synopsis: Covering arrays reduce large discrete configuration spaces while retaining interaction coverage; the proposed use is machine-by-sensor-by-weather-by-scenario configuration testing [f4332, f6818, f7233]. They can establish that every t-tuple of discrete values was tested at least once, but cannot establish coverage of interactions above t, continuous regions, or rates [f7234, f7235]. NIST provides an independent evidence base, but evidence that most bugs involve low-order interactions comes from software, and transfer to perception remains unproven [f7238, f7236]. Safety engineers therefore should not assume low-order combinations are sufficient for off-road collision avoidance [f4332]. Available tooling includes NIST ACTS, PICT and commercial test-design tools [f7237].
